title: Hierarchy-aware traffic anchoring for deferred canaries with phase-aware rollback oracle
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds hierarchy-aware traffic anchoring controller that enables deferred canaries with phase-aware rollback heuristics. Backwards compatible. Config opt-in via rollout.strategy.anchor_hierarchy.
body: Motivation: Large multi-service deployments require staged canaries that respect logical hierarchy and shared resources. This PR introduces a hierarchy-aware traffic anchoring controller that attaches canary phases to a stability anchor within a service hierarchy and uses phase-aware rollback heuristics to reduce noisy rollbacks across sibling cohorts. Key design: 1) Anchor graph model representing parent-child service relationships and resource affinity to compute safe traffic slots for deferred canaries 2) Phase windows with per-phase safety budgets and decaying anomaly thresholds 3) Rollback-oracle that considers sibling stability, global SLO burn rate, and momentum of metrics to make automated rollback decisions 4) Graceful handoff: anchor holds traffic while downstream verifies session-consistent swaps and drain hooks. Backwards compatibility: default rollout behavior unchanged unless rollout.strategy.anchor_hierarchy is enabled. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for anchor graph builder and allocator - [x] Integration tests for phased canary flow and session-affinity during swap - [x] E2E in perf-canary lab with synthetic load - [x] Console UI flags and rollout YAML schema bump - [x] Telemetry hooks for anchor and phase events Changes include lightweight controller, allocator, and operator-level telemetry plus YAML schema updates. Commits summary: commit 1: initial anchor graph and allocator implementation commit 2: phase window and safety budget logic commit 3: rollback-oracle prototype and tests commit 4: telemetry, metrics, and console flag wiring commit 5: docs and examples Updated files: controllers/anchor_controller.go controllers/allocator/graph.go controllers/rollback_oracle.go apis/rollout/v1alpha1/anchor_types.go docs/rollouts/anchor_hierarchy.md examples/rollouts/hierarchy-anchored-canary.yaml console/src/components/RolloutFlags.ts Files changed include controller logic, small schema addition, telemetry counters, and example manifests. Testing/CI: initial CI run showed flaky integ test (timeout) that was addressed by increasing test timeout and adding a deterministic seed; final CI status is pass with full unit, integration and lint. Performance: allocation adds negligible CPU (<2% at 2000 rps) and latency impact limited to controller reconciliation cycles; allocator caches computed slots for 60s and supports batched reconciliation to amortize work. Observability: new metrics redwood_rollout_anchor_allocations_total redwood_rollout_phase_transitions_total redwood_rollout_rollback_decisions{reason} and tracing spans for AnchorAllocate and RollbackDecision. Rollback behavior: oracle evaluates windowed deltas for latency/error/quality signals, computes sibling-aware severity, and will trigger staged rollback with holdpoints if sibling instability detected. Operational notes: - The feature is behind a feature flag rollout.strategy.anchor_hierarchy; enable per-namespace via annotation rollout.redwood.io/anchor-hierarchy=enabled - Default safety budgets are conservative and can be tuned via rollout.spec.anchor.safetyBudget - This controller requires no infra changes but recommends adding anchor graphs for services with shared dependencies Migration plan: gradual opt-in via examples/rollouts/hierarchy-anchored-canary.yaml followed by monitoring of anchor allocation metrics. Related work: builds on prior staged canary controllers and cohort-synchronous splitters but focuses on hierarchy constraints to avoid cascading rollbacks. Linear tickets: ENG-5982 (anchor controller) ENG-6013 (rollback oracle).
